newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan moves to block MPs from crossing floor.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan moves to block MPs from crossing floor.

text.p: Pakistan's National Assembly (lower house) passed a constitutional amendment on Tuesday designed to prevent parliamentarians from changing sides.
The 217-seat assembly voted 181-0 in favour of the bill, which was passed by the Senate (upper house) on Monday.
"This bill is intended to provide against defection of elected members with a view to obtaining a clean and honourable political state of affairs," the bill stated.
The change means a parliamentarian may lose his seat if he breaches party discipline, votes against the party line or abstains from voting in a way that runs against party policy.
Pakistani parliamentarians have in the past sometimes changed their loyalties for political advantage, amid accusations of bribery, intimidation and other malpractices.
"It was part of our manifesto," Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif told the National Assembly after the vote. "Our politics was tainted to a point where it had no parallel in the Third World."
